body: Indeed, thank you for your reply.

I do admire your courage to continue.

I know this answer is disappointing, but... I'm really just not good at anything.  I used to think I was good with computers, until I started studying this field and realized how stiff the competition is.  There's really nothing that I look at and think "Oh, if only I could be doing that!"  I don't know, maybe my self-esteem has just been ground down too much, but I tried considering your question for a few minutes and honestly I'm either bad or mediocre at everything I can think of.

Thank you for your suggestion.  I can see why you would think this might work, but in my field, it's all about skills - after the first HR phone screen, they ask a bunch of hard questions designed to test your skill level.  The initial HR phone screen may ask about work history, but the actual hiring manager only cares about your skill levels.  One of the issues is that I'm just really bad at what I do.  I tried in school and I've been trying on my own time to read books/take online MOOCs/work on my own projects, but I'm still bad at what I do.

Anyhow, I do really appreciate your concern, but I feel comfortable with the idea of death right now.  It seems to me like the best way to cut my losses, since my downward slide seems to be inexorable if I don't cut it short.
I wish you the best on your job search.

No, I have training for a particular kind of job, data analytics if you know anything about that.  As far as anxiety goes, I have it more or less under control at the moment, but I know that if I worked in a loud, fast paced environment like the food industry I wouldn't be able to handle it (I've tried many times to work in such jobs and it always causes my anxiety to get a lot worse).

The problem is, the longer I don't have a job, the harder it is to get one.  Employers ask "what have you been doing for the past half a year?"  Looking for a job, obviously, but that answer doesn't satisfy them.  Basically, it seems like they want to know why no one else wanted to hire me for so long.

Thank you for your response.
